details: A third U.S. aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, has arrived in the Middle East, significantly increasing the U.S. military presence in the region. This deployment comes as U.S. forces have conducted airstrikes on an Iranian missile site, and Iran has responded with drone attacks on U.S. military targets in Bahrain. The escalating tensions are fueling concerns about renewed conflict and broader market instability.
title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate Amid Military Buildup

details: The Trump administration has announced new restrictions to limit China's access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers, aiming to prevent Chinese AI developers from circumventing existing export controls by using overseas data centers. This move follows an alleged spy scandal involving AI giant Nvidia and a leadership change, adding uncertainty to the global tech sector and raising concerns about potential supply chain disruptions.
title: US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls on China

details: Bitcoin's price has fallen significantly, nearing $62,000, drawing comparisons to the 2022 crypto winter. This downturn is largely attributed to a rapid acceleration of stablecoin outflows, which are at their fastest pace since 2022, indicating a drain of liquidity from the cryptocurrency market. Mounting interest rate concerns and substantial outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs are also contributing to the deteriorating risk appetite among investors.
title: Bitcoin Plunges as Stablecoin Outflows Accelerate

details: The leaders of the United States, Australia, India, and Japan met for a Quad Leaders' Summit in Manila, reaffirming their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific. They expressed strong opposition to destabilizing actions and grave concerns about economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions. The summit aimed to secure critical supply chains and promote regional peace, stability, and prosperity.
title: Quad Leaders Address Economic Coercion in Indo-Pacific
